title: Does the count care how fast you pour?

data.source: The four rt- rooms: Jang (2026) tipping-bucket calibration, Mendeley Data; Allen Cell Types Database; glass-bead stick-slip, figshare (2026); Stagnaro and others (2021) drop-counter curves
data.licence: CC BY 4.0 (three sources); Allen Institute Terms of Use (one)

claim_kind: retrodiction on published data, mappings frozen first; a summary of four rooms
prediction: Drive one system at different rates: the amount it takes in between cuts stays the same (slope of log(amount per cut) on log(rate) inside -0.05 to +0.05), in each of three metered systems.
baseline: Each field's own model of its system, and a clock decoy (a cut every fixed time).
why: On the systems tested the count did not hold where the field's own model said it would not; one failed (a brain cell, by the leak its field already describes), one held to within about 8 % in a machine built to count, two could not be judged. By system: tipping bucket: partly (mixed), neuron: fails, laboratory fault: untestable, drop counter (not blind): untestable.

amended.reason:
AMENDMENT, 2026-11-19, AFTER THE SECOND CHECK (docs/CHECKS_RATE_SECOND_LOOK.md). The frozen docstring and the
summary rule are unchanged. The first summary (2026-11-18) counted two systems failing and one mixed, and said
the weakest outcome weighed 22.1 to 1. The second checker showed the fault's `fails` could not be supported (one
run per speed), and rt-003 was withdrawn to `untestable`. By the same frozen rule the summary is still `partly`
(mixed), but the count behind it is now one fails, one mixed, one untestable (and the drop counter, not blind,
untestable). The "22.1 to 1" was the fault's weight and is removed.

phoenix_status: R2 is marked ASSUMPTION and R3 is marked RESULT in CORE/MATHEMATICS.md ("This identity is standard path-length arithmetic, not evidence for a new physical law"). README.md records: "The two clocks failed as an empirical hypothesis."
